Today's the day! Welcome to Horizons Alternative Provision Academy. We are proud to officially open our doors and begin an exciting new journey, providing high-quality alternative education for children and young people across Reading, Bracknell, Newbury, Wokingham and South Oxfordshire. As part of Maiden Erlegh Trust, Horizons brings together expertise, opportunity and ambition to help every learner thrive. We can't wait to welcome all of our children, young people and families through our doors as they begin their Horizons journey with us. Welcome to Horizons
Horizons Opens its Doors
We are delighted to announce the official opening of Horizons Alternative Provision Academy!Created by Maiden Erlegh Trust so more children and young people across Reading and Bracknell can access high-quality alternative educational pathways, Horizons brings together the established expertise of Cranbury College with a new primary site in Bracknell, new vocational courses at Maiden Erlegh School and a dedicated tuition team.Across five purposeful pathways, high expectations and high challenge are matched with expert support and learning relevant to young people’s lives, interests and future. Children and young people can discover what they are good at, build confidence, develop skills, achieve qualifications and open up future opportunities.Horizons is learning worth turning up for.We can’t wait to welcome existing and new families!Explore our new website and brochure to discover Horizons.

Horizons Life
Careers
Careers, Work Experience and Work Related Learning
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) is an important part of learning at Horizons, helping young people understand the opportunities available to them and make informed choices about their future.
We provide activities, experiences and guidance that help young people develop skills, explore their interests and strengths, and prepare for their next steps into further education, training, apprenticeships or work.
Equality and diversity considerations are embedded throughout our careers programme.
Our aims for CEIAG are:
Careers education at Horizons is about more than learning about jobs. It helps young people understand the world of work, develop practical and interpersonal skills, explore different opportunities and prepare confidently for their future.
In this section, you will find useful links and information about careers, further education and training, including careers fairs, volunteering and work experience. Horizons also has partnership status with Adviza, giving young people access to impartial careers guidance through our careers adviser, Anna Finlason.
Please find the Horizons Provider Access Policy below.
If you would like to discuss our careers programme further, please contact our Careers and Destinations Lead, Mr Will Baggley, at w.baggley@maidenerleghtrust.org.

pageCache.text:
Why Horizons?
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Horizons Alternative Provision Academy
As Headteacher, I am incredibly pleased to welcome you to Horizons and excited about what we offer children and young people.
At Horizons, we believe every child and young person is important and has the right to a great education. Every learner is different, and our role is to provide learning that brings out their best: learning that is relevant, purposeful and opens up opportunities. Learning worth turning up for.
We believe in every young person’s capacity to learn, achieve and create opportunities. That belief sits at the heart of Horizons and everything we do.
Learning worth turning up for.
Five pathways - shared ambition
Across our five purposeful pathways, we combine high expectations and high challenge with expert support, creating different ways for children and young people to make meaningful progress and achieve. Our pathways span Reading and Bracknell and bring together the established expertise of Cranbury College with new opportunities for children and young people.
Learning at Horizons combines National Curriculum and vocational learning with rich personal development and enrichment. We want children and young people to discover what they are good at, build confidence, develop skills, achieve qualifications, become more independent and prepare for what comes next.
Horizons builds connections that create a sense of belonging. We want children and young people to enjoy learning, recognise their progress and feel positive about what they can achieve.
Our ambition for every young person
My ambition for Horizons is simple: for every child and young person to be known and valued, to experience learning that brings out their best, and to leave us believing in what they can achieve.
My ambition for Horizons is simple: for every child and young person to be known and valued, to experience learning that brings out their best, and to leave us believing in what they can achieve.
The strength of Maiden Erlegh Trust
One of the things I value as Headteacher is the strength we gain from being part of Maiden Erlegh Trust. We are part of a family of schools known for high-quality, inclusive education, with a wealth of expertise across different educational settings. Our staff can work, learn and collaborate with colleagues across the Trust, strengthening what we offer and creating more opportunities for our children and young people.
We look forward to welcoming you
When children, young people and their families join Horizons, they will always receive a warm welcome and can expect to be understood, valued and supported.
We look forward to welcoming you.
Claire Wilmott Headteacher

Remote Learning

For further information please contact our main office on horizons@maidenerleghtrust.org.
